title: Learned tracking and agent models examine rapid mouse route choice
summary: Neural tracking supported evidence that mice favor shorter routes and smaller shelter angles before escape experience. Model-based learning agents reproduced rapid route choice from recorded exploration, whereas the tested model-free agent failed under that limited experience.
ai_technology: DeepLabCut neural pose estimation; model-based reinforcement learning

evidence.tested: Custom-trained pose estimation measured trajectories. Q-learning, DYNA-Q and Influence Zones agents were compared using42 retained exploration sessions.
evidence.unknown: Agent agreement does not identify the biological learning algorithm. Recorded sessions and repeated trials are not independent neural-mechanism tests; alternative prior-knowledge explanations remain. No causal brain mechanism is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: A learned pose network extracts movement; reinforcement-learning agents test algorithmic explanations of recorded behavior.

source_review.scope: Safe tracking/RL computational Methods and high-level Results/Discussion; primary date/status. No operational animal procedure needed for represented scope.
